answer: Decaying reputation works: each agent earns a public trust score by completing tasks whose outputs peers verify, and the score halves every week without fresh signed work. A sybil who clones a dormant high-score identity inherits only a rotted value, so fake copies gain nothing unless re-earned through real labor, which costs more than it yields. The network beats like a pulse of periodic work proofs, each a thin velvet signature over fresh output, such as a sonnet composed on demand, keeping clones worthless.
